author: reek
body: Archiving reclaims the live log, and does not touch the tree.

author: reek
body: A base that copies a range and leaves it in place reclaims nothing. This is the half with teeth: it shrinks the log, and it is the half that can destroy a repository if the cut is chosen wrong.

author: reek
body: Three editions of a.codex, then one of b.codex. Only the third edition of a.codex is current, so the first two may leave -- and they sit at the bottom of the log, so a prefix cut can reach them. The third edition is current and stops the cut there, which is the prefix rule doing its job: everything below the cut goes, and the first fact that must stay ends it.

author: reek
body: THE INVARIANT, and the reason this test exists: archive, rebuild, and the TREE is unchanged. Not the history -- wi-works loses the archived editions, which is the entire point of moving them, and they are in the base, still addressable and still verifying.

author: reek
body: The .disk sidecar is load-bearing. Without a disk attached codex-vm drops every write and reads return zeros, and a store with no facts in it archives nothing while agreeing with itself about everything.

author: reek
body: The artifact decompresses to a fact log, byte for byte, so the first archived entry starts at offset zero and its first 32 bytes are that entry's header hash. Reading them back out proves archiving MOVED the work rather than dropping it.

author: reek
body: That header hash is the hash of the stored LINE -- the whole hash|path|...|len|content record -- and NOT the hash of the source the line carries. The two are different and it is the same distinction that makes DiskFacts' own map useless for finding a work: it is an index of records. A first cut of this check compared the header against the WORK's hash and failed for exactly that reason. So the expected value is built the way the writer built it: sign the same definition again and hash its wire line. Signing is deterministic, so the line is byte-identical to the archived one.

author: reek
body: The claim "an archived work is still retrievable" is only worth as much as a function that retrieves one. This asks the base for the superseded edition by the hash the tree used to point at, and checks the SOURCE comes back -- not that some bytes came back.

author: reek
body: And it is still a signed fact after the round trip through compression: the same verification the import gate applies, applied to a work that has been archived, compressed, expanded and parsed back.
